passages.text: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; devout men are swept away, while no one considers that the righteous are guided from the presence of evil.
passages.sermon:
The righteous man dies.
No one pays attention.
No one cares in their heart.
Faithful people disappear.
No one understands why.
God removes the righteous to protect them from evil.
passages.original: הַצַּדִּ֣יק אָבָ֔ד וְאֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֣ם עַל־ לֵ֑ב וְאַנְשֵׁי־ חֶ֤סֶד נֶֽאֱסָפִים֙ בְּאֵ֣ין מֵבִ֔ין כִּֽי־ מִפְּנֵ֥י הָרָעָ֖ה נֶאֱסַ֥ף הַצַּדִּֽיק׃

passages.text: Those who walk uprightly enter into peace; they find rest, lying down in death.
passages.sermon:
Those who live upright lives find peace.
They enter into rest.
They lie down in death.
They rest in peace because they walked in honesty and righteousness.
passages.original: יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־ מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “But come here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He calls them to come near.
He calls them sons of a sorceress.
He says they are children of an adulterer.
He says they are children of a prostitute.
passages.original: וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ־ הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה זֶ֥רַע מְנָאֵ֖ף וַתִּזְנֶֽה׃

passages.text: Whom are you mocking? At whom do you snarl and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of deceit, who burn with lust among the oaks, under every luxuriant tree, who slaughter your children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?
passages.sermon:
You are children of transgression.
You are offspring of deceit.
You mock others.
You snarl at others.
You stick out your tongue at others.
You burn with lust among the oaks.
You burn with lust under every luxuriant tree.
You slaughter your children in the valleys.
You slaughter your children under the clefts of the rocks.
passages.original: עַל־ מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ עַל־ מִ֛י תַּרְחִ֥יבוּ פֶ֖ה תַּאֲרִ֣יכוּ לָשׁ֑וֹן הֲלֽוֹא־ אַתֶּ֥ם יִלְדֵי־ פֶ֖שַׁע זֶ֥רַע שָֽׁקֶר׃ הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ בָּֽאֵלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־ עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֑ן שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י הַיְלָדִים֙ בַּנְּחָלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת סְעִפֵ֥י הַסְּלָעִֽים׃

passages.text: Your portion is among the smooth stones of the valley; indeed, they are your lot. Even to them you have poured out a drink offering and offered a grain offering. Should I relent because of these?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He describes their actions.
You have chosen your portion among the smooth stones in the valley.
These stones are your inheritance.
You have poured out drink offerings to these stones.
You have offered grain offerings to them.
God asks a question.
Should I comfort you because of these actions?
passages.original: בְּחַלְּקֵי־ נַ֣חַל חֶלְקֵ֔ךְ הֵ֥ם הֵ֖ם גּוֹרָלֵ֑ךְ גַּם־ לָהֶ֞ם שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֙סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה הַ֥עַל אֵ֖לֶּה אֶנָּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: On a high and lofty hill you have made your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifices.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned away from God.
They chose to worship idols.
They went to a high and lofty hill.
They made their bed there.
They went up to that place.
They offered sacrifices there.
passages.original: עַ֤ל הַר־ גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ וְנִשָּׂ֔א שַׂ֖מְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵ֑ךְ גַּם־ שָׁ֥ם עָלִ֖ית לִזְבֹּ֥חַ זָֽבַח׃

passages.text: Behind the door and doorpost you have set up your memorial. Forsaking Me, you uncovered your bed; you climbed up and opened it wide. And you have made a pact with those whose bed you have loved; you have gazed upon their nakedness.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned away from God.
They set up their memorial behind the door and doorpost.
They did not honor God in their homes.
They left God and chose other ways.
They uncovered their bed.
They climbed up and opened it wide.
They made a pact with others.
They loved the beds of those others.
They looked upon their nakedness.
passages.original: וְאַחַ֤ר הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ וְהַמְּזוּזָ֔ה שַׂ֖מְתְּ זִכְרוֹנֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י מֵאִתִּ֞י גִּלִּ֣ית וַֽתַּעֲלִ֗י הִרְחַ֤בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵךְ֙ וַתִּכְרָת־ לָ֣ךְ מֵהֶ֔ם אָהַ֥בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבָ֖ם יָ֥ד חָזִֽית׃

passages.text: You went to Molech with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You have sent your envoys a great distance; you have descended even to Sheol itself.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned away from God.
They went to Molech.
They brought oil to Molech.
They used many perfumes for Molech.
They sent their messengers far away.
They went down as far as Sheol.
passages.original: וַתָּשֻׁ֤רִי לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וַתַּרְבִּ֖י רִקֻּחָ֑יִךְ וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֤י צִרַ֙יִךְ֙ עַד־ מֵ֣רָחֹ֔ק וַתַּשְׁפִּ֖ילִי עַד־ שְׁאֽוֹל׃

passages.text: You are wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, “There is no hope!” You found renewal of your strength; therefore you did not grow weak.
passages.sermon:
You traveled many roads.
You became tired from your journeys.
You did not say, "There is no hope."
You found new strength in your own hand.
Because of this, you did not grow weak.
passages.original: בְּרֹ֤ב דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ יָגַ֔עַתְּ לֹ֥א אָמַ֖רְתְּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ חַיַּ֤ת יָדֵךְ֙ מָצָ֔את עַל־ כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א חָלִֽית׃

passages.text: Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lied and failed to remember Me or take this to heart? Is it not because I have long been silent that you do not fear Me?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God asks them a question.
God says, “Who made you afraid?”
God says, “Who caused you to fear?”
God says, “You lied because of this fear.”
God says, “You did not remember Me.”
God says, “You did not keep Me in your heart.”
God says, “I have been silent for a long time.”
God says, “You do not fear Me because of My silence.”
passages.original: וְאֶת־ מִ֞י דָּאַ֤גְתְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּ֣י תְכַזֵּ֔בִי וְאוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔רְתְּ לֹא־ שַׂ֖מְתְּ עַל־ לִבֵּ֑ךְ הֲלֹ֨א אֲנִ֤י מַחְשֶׁה֙ וּמֵ֣עֹלָ֔ם וְאוֹתִ֖י לֹ֥א תִירָֽאִי׃

passages.text: I will expose your righteousness and your works, and they will not profit you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks.
God will show your righteousness.
God will show your deeds.
Your righteousness will not help you.
Your deeds will not help you.
passages.original: אֲנִ֥י אַגִּ֖יד צִדְקָתֵ֑ךְ וְאֶֽת־ מַעֲשַׂ֖יִךְ וְלֹ֥א יוֹעִילֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: When you cry out, let your companies of idols deliver you! Yet the wind will carry off all of them, a breath will take them away. But he who seeks refuge in Me will inherit the land and possess My holy mountain.”
passages.sermon:
You have trusted in idols.
You have gathered many idols together.
You will cry out for help.
Let your idols save you.
The wind will carry away all your idols.
A breath will take them all away.
Anyone who seeks refuge in Me will remain safe.
He will inherit the land.
He will possess My holy mountain.
passages.original: בְּזַֽעֲקֵךְ֙ יַצִּילֻ֣ךְ קִבּוּצַ֔יִךְ וְאֶת־ כֻּלָּ֥ם יִשָּׂא־ ר֖וּחַ יִקַּח־ הָ֑בֶל וְהַחוֹסֶ֥ה בִי֙ יִנְחַל־ אֶ֔רֶץ וְיִירַ֖שׁ הַר־ קָדְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: And it will be said, “Build it up, build it up, prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He commands others to act.
He says, “Build up the road.
Build it up.
Prepare the way for My people.
Remove every obstacle from their path.”
passages.original: וְאָמַ֥ר סֹֽלּוּ־ סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ־ דָ֑רֶךְ הָרִ֥ימוּ מִכְשׁ֖וֹל מִדֶּ֥רֶךְ עַמִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite.
passages.sermon:
God is high and lifted up.
God inhabits eternity.
God’s name is Holy.
God dwells in a high and holy place.
God also dwells with people who are oppressed.
God dwells with people who are humble in spirit.
God restores the spirit of the lowly.
God revives the heart of the contrite.
passages.original: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א שֹׁכֵ֥ן עַד֙ וְקָד֣וֹשׁ שְׁמ֔וֹ מָר֥וֹם וְקָד֖וֹשׁ אֶשְׁכּ֑וֹן וְאֶת־ דַּכָּא֙ וּשְׁפַל־ ר֔וּחַ לְהַחֲיוֹת֙ ר֣וּחַ שְׁפָלִ֔ים וּֽלְהַחֲי֖וֹת לֵ֥ב נִדְכָּאִֽים׃

passages.text: For I will not accuse you forever, nor will I always be angry; for then the spirit of man would grow weak before Me, with the breath of those I have made.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God is high and lifted up.
God inhabits eternity.
God’s name is Holy.
God says, “I will not accuse you forever.
I will not always be angry.
If I did, the spirit of man would grow weak before Me.
I made the breath of every person.
I created all people.
I do not want to destroy those I have made.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְעוֹלָם֙ אָרִ֔יב וְלֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אֶקְּצ֑וֹף כִּי־ ר֙וּחַ֙ מִלְּפָנַ֣י יַֽעֲט֔וֹף וּנְשָׁמ֖וֹת אֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי׃

passages.text: I was enraged by his sinful greed, so I struck him and hid My face in anger; yet he kept turning back to the desires of his heart.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and eternal.
God lives in a high and holy place.
God also cares for the humble and the oppressed.
God saw a man’s sinful greed.
God became angry because of this sin.
God struck the man.
God hid His face from the man in anger.
The man did not change.
The man kept following the desires of his own heart.
passages.original: בַּעֲוֺ֥ן בִּצְע֛וֹ קָצַ֥פְתִּי וְאַכֵּ֖הוּ הַסְתֵּ֣ר וְאֶקְצֹ֑ף וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ שׁוֹבָ֖ב בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have seen his ways, but I will heal him; I will guide him and restore comfort to him and his mourners, bringing praise to their lips. Peace, peace to those far and near,” says the LORD, “and I will heal them.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees every person’s ways.
The LORD sees what each person does.
The LORD chooses to heal the person who has gone astray.
The LORD guides that person.
The LORD restores comfort to that person.
The LORD gives comfort to those who mourn for him.
The LORD creates praise on their lips.
The LORD says, “Peace, peace to those who are far away.”
The LORD says, “Peace, peace to those who are near.”
The LORD promises, “I will heal them.”
passages.original: דְּרָכָ֥יו רָאִ֖יתִי וְאֶרְפָּאֵ֑הוּ וְאַנְחֵ֕הוּ וַאֲשַׁלֵּ֧ם נִֽחֻמִ֛ים ל֖וֹ וְלַאֲבֵלָֽיו׃ בּוֹרֵ֖א נוּב שְׂפָתָ֑יִם שָׁל֨וֹם׀ שָׁל֜וֹם לָרָח֧וֹק וְלַקָּר֛וֹב אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה וּרְפָאתִֽיו׃

passages.text: But the wicked are like the storm-tossed sea, for it cannot be still, and its waves churn up mire and muck.
passages.sermon:
The wicked act with evil in their hearts.
The wicked are like the sea during a storm.
The sea cannot rest.
The sea is always moving and tossing.
The waves of the sea stir up mud and dirt.
The wicked cannot find peace.
Their actions bring trouble and impurity.
passages.original: וְהָרְשָׁעִ֖ים כַּיָּ֣ם נִגְרָ֑שׁ כִּ֤י הַשְׁקֵט֙ לֹ֣א יוּכָ֔ל וַיִּגְרְשׁ֥וּ מֵימָ֖יו רֶ֥פֶשׁ וָטִֽיט׃

passages.text: “There is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.”
passages.sermon: God speaks clearly.\r\nGod says, “There is no peace for the wicked.”
